newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian base metals steady in limited activity.
newsitem.headline: Indian base metals steady in limited activity.

text.p: All the base metals remained steady amid limited activity on the local market on Monday, dealers said.
Fresh industrial demand remained sluggish but a recent upsurge in the global market combined with limited supplies to keep offerings at low ebb.
Copper was quiet at 13,900 rupees per quintal after gaining 50 rupees on Saturday. Zinc was steady at 8,050 rupees per quintal as was lead at 4,100 rupees per quintal.
"State-owned agencies have kept selling prices unchanged for the second half of the current month after the hike announced in the first half," one broker said.

In the first half Hindustan Copper raised prices by 5,000/6,000 rupees per tonne and Hindustan Zinc by 1,500/2,000 rupees per tonne. Tin was steady at 30,900 rupees per quintal after a loss of 500 rupees last week while nickel was quiet at 36,200 rupees per quintal after losing 300 rupees last week.
Aluminium was steady at 7,700 rupees per quintal but sentiment was firm on expectations that local producers might hike prices shortly.
